description: Leonidas of Sparta married Gorgo, the daughter and only known child of King Cleomenes I, probably sometime in the late 6th or early 5th century BC. The marriage joined Leonidas, a member of the Agiad royal house and Cleomenes’ half-brother, to the king’s heiress, strengthening Leonidas’ dynastic position before he eventually succeeded to the throne. Ancient sources preserve little about their actual betrothal ceremony, but Spartan marriage customs were generally austere and closely tied to family, inheritance, and civic expectations. Gorgo later became one of the best-known Spartan women in Greek tradition, remembered for her intelligence and political awareness as well as for being the wife of Leonidas.
